This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. Hill's Pick: Brock Bowers Over 76.5 Receiving Yards Chargers @ Seahawks The Chargers look broken offensively and could not defeat the Bills last week despite their defense forcing five turnovers. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Lions (-2.5) vs Patriots: O/U 51.5 The Lions and Patriots will meet in Munich, Germany, with a potential shootout on our hands. Last week, Green Bay torched New England’s secondary for almost 400 passing yards, and the Patriots face Detroit, which hasn’t had to throw the last two games. Jared Goff has thrown 25 pass attempts in each of his past two games against the Dolphins and Vikings and gone under 200 yards. Goff hasn’t gone under 200 passing yards in back-to-back games since 2024. Before the previous two games, Goff threw at least 30 passes in six straight and 38 or more in three. This is a spot where I think he clears 30 and could approach 40 pass attempts. The Patriots run the second-most man coverage (28.5%), and that opens the door for this Lions offense. Plenty of tackle opportunities for Miami's defense, and in particular a linebacker like Brooks. But the model knows all that and says this line is just far too high. Just last week Miami was massive underdogs to the 49ers and Brooks recorded just three combined tackles. I would bet this down to -150.

I have seven picks I like this week, including player props on Patrick Mahomes , Drake Maye , and Tony Pollard , plus three spreads picks for the 1 PM Eastern games. Best of luck, happy November, and enjoy your day! Vikings at Lions (-3): O/U 46.5 I said Monday of this week on NBC that this was the no-brainer of the week. It’s a miracle that the Minnesota Vikings are the lone undefeated team in the NFL, and to me, they are the most overrated team. In the last four games, Minnesota has beaten Tampa Bay, Miami, New Orleans, and Indianapolis; those teams are a combined 7-20. Last season, the Vikings swept the Lions in the regular season, and adding Kyler Murray likely doesn’t equate to another sweep over Detroit. Murray ranks 21st and 26th in passer rating against man and zone coverage, 28th in blitzed completion percentage (54.8%), and 26th in play-action completion percentage (54.9%). On early downs, Minnesota ranks in success rate, while Detroit is first. Going score for score on the road as an underdog with Jared Goff and the Lions doesn’t seem plausible to me. I like Detroit -3 at -120 odds. Titans at Bengals (-12.5): O/U 46.5 Tony Pollard had a season-high 129 rushing yards on 25 carries and tied a career-high with three rushing touchdowns. It was a great day for Pollard, but the Titans lost at the buzzer 27-24 to the Browns. Now, Tennessee goes on the road as double-digit underdogs in Cincinnati. Not a recipe for success. Last week, Pollard had an amazing game script to be fed, maybe the best he’s had all year, but I don’t see it this week, especially going up against Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen . The Bengals held Derrick Henry to 45 rushing yards on 17 carries last week, and with Cam Ward striking no fear in the Bengals’ hearts, I’d think Cincy stacks the box and attempt to take Pollard out of the equation. I went Under 65.5 rushing yards on Pollard and would go down to 60.5. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 65.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Browns at Steelers (-3.5): O/U 38.5 I still can’t believe my eyes and ears regarding the Cleveland Browns being 5-2! But all good things must come to an end, right? All five of Cleveland’s wins have come by four or fewer points, and they needed a walkoff field goal to beat the Titans in Tennessee and the same at home against the Ravens in the last two weeks. Cleveland has been playing with fire recently, while the Steelers were spotted flying back from Paris playing with ice. Aaron Rodgers was wearing chains that cost more than my house and probably yours too on that flight back from the NFL’s first-ever game in Paris. Rodgers said it was his favorite road flight of his lengthy NFL career, and the Steelers are starting to hit their stride with three-straight wins following the loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers traveling back to an immediate game is worrisome because the last eight teams that played in London, then a game in the States the following week, went 0-8 ATS! However, the Browns haven’t swept the Steelers in the regular season since 1988. It’s a revenge spot for Pittsburgh, and if you’ve seen the back-and-forth between Cam Heyward and Jared Verse this week, then you know it’s going to be a classic AFC North slugfest. Give me Pittsburgh at home -3.5. I’d prefer a -3, but the sportsbooks are playing more defense than ever this season. Pick: Steelers -3.5 (1 unit) Falcons at Bucs (-2.5): O/U Tampa Bay got that Baker bump last week! Baker Mayfield came back from injury and Tampa Bay looked inspired. The Bucs rattled Bryce Young last week and destroyed his confidence turning three turnovers into 17 of the teams 43 points. This week won’t be so easy hosting Atlanta in a letdown spot off the hype. Mayfield only threw the ball 11 times, so we truly don’t know how healthy he is or how effective he will be, but we know what to expect from Atlanta. The Falcons have the fifth-best offensive success rate since Michael Penix has taken over, and he’s gotten the ball out quick with 50% of his passes coming within 2.5 seconds (fourth-best). That could be the key against a blitz and pressure heavy Bucs defense. Tampa Bay loads the box with eight or more players at the second-highest clip (22.1%) and blitzes 40.4% of the time when doing so, which ranks fifth-most. I’d expect a lot of screens, draws, and quick throws to offeset the Bucs defense, while Atlanta likely brings pressure and tries to hit Mayfield as many times as possible to truly test his health and conditioning. Give me Atlanta. Pick: Falcons +2.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Patriots (-7) at Dolphins: O/U 43.5 Last season, Drake Maye completed 33-of-41 (80.5%) passes for 421 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions over two wins against Miami. Maye even added 72 rushing yards and another score on 15 carries in those two outings. This Miami defense is even less menacing than last year. The Dolphins have four interceptions on the season, and two came in Week 1 against Kirk Cousins , with another last week courtesy of Geno Smith . When Joe Burrow , Patrick Mahomes , Brock Purdy , and Kyler Murray played Miami, that group averaged 242.5 passing yards against the Dolphins and combined for eight touchdown passes to one interception. The Vikings’ defense and special teams are elite. Minnesota just needs an offense that can move the ball enough to score points, so the defense doesn’t have to be perfect to win games. The defense has also played better than expected, shutting down nearly every offense it has faced this season. I like the Vikings to cover this game for a few reasons. For starters, just having Cousins in the lineup will reinvigorate the Vikings, and it wouldn’t surprise me to see Justin Jefferson have his best game of the season. I also like the matchup of the Vikings’ defense against the Packers’ offensive line, which is mediocre. Minnesota's pressure packages will be difficult to handle.
